title: Adaptive burst fallback on lease-loss causing reserved-pool shortfalls
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Multiple customers experienced brief but repeated capacity shortfalls in Dedicated reserved pools during regional network flaps. Symptoms: sudden inability to acquire burst capacity despite apparent headroom, followed by rapid token drain and request shedding. Initial triage suggests a lease-manager race where transient lease-loss events are not triggering conservative fallback admission; allocator treats transient lease return as permanent causing ledger miscount and reduced burst supply. This ticket tracks the detection, patch, and staged rollout of an adaptive fallback path that tolerates short lease-loss windows and safely reclaims headroom for high-priority tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator correctly reconciles burst ledger after transient lease-loss events (unit tests + e2e)
No customer-facing rejected-burst incidents in synthetic surge test (3 region failover scenarios)
Telemetry shows no >10% headroom desync post-fix during a 48h replay of last-month burst traffic
Canary rollout completes with zero Sev1 regressions and automated rollback triggers validated
steps_taken: 11/20: initial alert from SRE after two customer escalations (Acme/FinHealth) during AZ network blips
11/20: created minimal reproducer in staging using lease-invalidation injector; observed ledger undercount after lease rebind
11/21: captured detailed allocator/lease-manager traces and KV audit logs; attached to ticket
11/21: disabled strict 'hard-evict-on-lease-loss' path in a staging harness to confirm mitigation
11/22: prototype fix implemented to add conservative grace window and explicit ledger reconciliation pass
11/23: unit tests added for lease-rebind scenarios and race windows; integration tests failing on older kernel optimizer path
11/24: PR opened for review and initial canary plan drafted
proposed_fix: Introduce a two-part change: (1) allocator changes to treat short lease-loss events as 'transient' for a configurable grace period (default 30s) and queue conservative admission rather than hard-evict; (2) reconciliation job that periodically validates burst ledger against live leases and performs idempotent corrections. Also add telemetry counters for lease-loss, reconciliation events, and a health check metric that will gate canary promotion.
rollout_plan: Stage A: deploy to staging with lease-injector enabled; run synthetic surges and AZ partition replay
Stage B: canary rollout to 5% of Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 (non-critical tenants) for 6h with extended tracing
Stage C: expand to 25% and monitor 48h; enable automatic rollback on SLO violation or increased request latency
Stage D: full rollout across regions with rollout-graph and post-deploy reconciliation sweep

postmortem_notes: If fix proves effective we will convert this ticket into a postmortem template summarizing root cause, code change, monitoring improvements, and customer outreach. Preliminary root cause points to race between lease-manager timeout and allocator hard-evict path; organizational follow-up: add SLA for lease-manager healing and review default grace threshold across Dedicated subsystems.
ops_runbook_snippet: If a canary shows increased rejected-burst errors: immediately pause rollout and run reconciliation job with --force-check;
If headroom desync persists after reconciliation: rollback runtime change, and escalate to allocator-leads and SRE;
For customer comms: notify affected tenants with summary + ETA within 30 minutes of confirmed mitigation
